newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA FIRST SLOVENE TO WIN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-PETERKA FIRST SLOVENE TO WIN WORLD CUP.

text.p: Teenager Primoz Peterka became the first Slovenian to clinch the ski jumping World Cup title with a fourth place in the season's penultimate event on Saturday.

Peterka, 18 and in only his second winter on the World Cup tour, leads the overall standings with an unbeatable 1,322 points to German Dieter Thoma's 1,190 after the first of back-to-back ski flying competitions at this northern Slovenian resort.
"If I have a few more seasons like this one then I will start thinking that I must have been born under a lucky star," said Peterka. "A big stone has fallen from my heart."
Despite clinching the overall title just a day after bruising himself following a tumble in training, Peterka was disappointed with his fourth place after jumps of 196.50 and 186 metres.

"I was a bit scared during the first jump today because of yesterday's accident. I was only thinking about landing safely," he explained. "Our team psychologist kept telling me to think about other things."
Thoma, the only other ski jumper to have threatened Peterka in the overall standings, finished a disappointing sixth on Saturday.
The day's victory went to Japan's Takanobu Okabe who posted jumps of 197.50 metres and 207 metres -- the longest-ever ski flying jump recorded in World Cup competition.

"I'm in very good shape at the moment. I want to repeat this good performance tomorrow in order to win the ski flying World Cup," said Okabe, who leads the flying standings with 260 points ahead of Peterka on 210.

Okabe's compatriot Kazuyoshi Funaki, currently third in the overall standings with 973 points, took second place with jumps of 190.50 and 204 metres, ahead of Finland's Jani Soininen who sailed to 203.50 and 187 metres.
In training earlier on Saturday, Norway's Lasse Ottesen broke his compatriot Espen Bredesen's 1994 world ski flying record of 209 metres when he soared to 212 metres.
